initial_prompt: Tell me about vaccines and how they work.

messages.content: Tell me about vaccines and how they work.

Vaccines train your immune system to recognize and fight specific diseases without you having to get sick first. They typically contain weakened or inactive parts of a pathogen (like a virus or bacteria), or instructions for your cells to make a harmless piece of it. When you get vaccinated, your immune system responds by creating antibodies and memory cells - essentially learning to recognize that particular threat. If you're later exposed to the actual disease, your immune system can mount a rapid, effective response because it's already prepared, often preventing illness entirely or making it much milder.
